subject: Hosted runtime deep-dive: SDKs, streaming & tool-calling — schedule
messages:
From: Nina Shah <nina@medflow.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-22T08:03:00-07:00
Subject: Request: hosted runtime deep-dive for streaming & function/tool calling

Hi Logan —

We’re kicking off an evaluation of hosted inference options and would like a technical deep-dive focused on:
- client SDKs (python/node) and recommended integration patterns
- streaming (server->client) and best-effort latency/throughput tradeoffs
- function/tool calling + security boundaries (what data leaves our VPC)
- runtime observability (token-level traces, KV cache visibility)

Can your team run a 60–90 minute session the week of Apr 27? Our preferred windows (PT):
- Tue Apr 28, 10:00–12:00 or 14:00–16:00
- Thu Apr 30, 09:00–11:00

We’re bringing our platform lead (Julian Park) and an ops engineer. Goal is to validate integration approach and surface any blockers for a POC.

Thanks — happy to share a short list of questions in advance if that helps.

—Nina
Nina Shah
Head of Product, MedFlow AI
[nina@medflow.ai]

From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
To: Nina Shah <nina@medflow.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-22T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: hosted runtime deep-dive for streaming & function/tool calling

Hi Nina —

Thanks for the note. We’d love to run this. We can do a 90-minute deep-dive to make sure we cover both architecture and hands-on examples (SDK snippets + a short live demo of streaming). Proposed slots (PT):
- Tue Apr 28, 10:30–12:00
- Thu Apr 30, 09:00–10:30

Quick agenda I’m proposing (I’ll attach a one-pager):
1) Intros & success criteria (5m)
2) SDK integration patterns + auth (15m)
3) Streaming demo + sample client (20m)
4) Function/tool calling & security boundaries (20m)
5) Ops/observability: tracing, token cost, caching (20m)
6) Q&A / next steps (10m)

Karthik will cover the streaming/demo and Monica will take the ops/observability section. If you want us to focus more on latency SLOs or cost profiling, tell us and we’ll adjust.

I’ve attached a short proposed agenda and our internal "invoke" playbook that answers common security questions.

Attachments:
- proposed-agenda.md
- redwood-invoke-playbook.pdf

If any of those slots work, I’ll send a calendar invite with a short pre-read.

Cheers,
Logan Wright
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
logan_wright@redwood.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Nina Shah <nina@medflow.ai>
Date: 2026-04-22T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: hosted runtime deep-dive for streaming & function/tool calling

+1 on the 90-minute option. A couple of operational asks from my side that we should clarify before the session so we can come prepared:
- preferred client language for the live snippet (python or node)? we can demo both but will be faster if they pick one
- expected sequence lengths / typical prompt sizes and expected concurrency (so we can show batching/latency tradeoffs)
- whether they need an internal-only rollout (VPC/private) vs hosted API evaluation — affects tool-calling security explanation

I’ll add a short demo plan to the calendar invite (live streaming from a small Node client -> Redwood hosted runtime + a tool call showing a secure webhook).

Calendar link for the tentative slot (to be updated once confirmed): https://calendar.google.com/event?eid=abc123

—Karthik
Engineering Lead, Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Hi Logan & team —

Thanks — Thu Apr 30 at 09:00–10:30 PT works for us (we’ll need 90 minutes). I’ve added Julian (ops lead) to the thread. A couple of requests so we’re productive:
- can you share the calendar invite with a Google Meet link and recording enabled?
- please include any short pre-reads (SDK snippets / sample request shapes) so our engineers can scan ahead
- we’ll send a small list of scoped questions by EOD tomorrow (e.g., KV cache size limits, max tokens per request, recommended retry/backoff patterns)

Thanks — looking forward to it.

—Nina
Head of Product, MedFlow AI
